Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 37
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Psychologist
  trauma_type: Rape
  pcl5: 61

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Locked Spaces: Being in a locked or confined room, Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence, Male Presence: Being alone with men
  Threat: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room, Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
  Negative Appraisals: Hopelessness: I have no future, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me, Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

Vignette:
Kofi, a 37-year-old African male psychologist, has been grappling with the aftermath of a traumatic rape incident that occurred six months ago. The event happened during a professional conference in Las Vegas where Kofi was staying at a hotel alone. One evening, he found himself unable to leave his room due to a locked door and had no way to contact anyone for help when a man entered his room and attacked him. This experience has left deep scars that manifest in various ways throughout his daily life. Since the incident, being in any confined space, such as a hotel room or even his office with the door closed, triggers intense anxiety for Kofi. He remembers vividly how he felt trapped during the attack and now experiences a sense of dread whenever he finds himself in similar situations. At work, he makes sure to keep his office door slightly ajar, even when consulting with clients, which has started to affect his professional relationships as he feels uncomfortable engaging fully without this perceived safety measure. Kofi’s occupation as a psychologist places him in frequent interaction with men, including male colleagues and patients. Being alone with men now triggers acute anxiety, often leading to hypervigilance and avoidance behaviors. He avoids one-on-one meetings whenever possible and tries to schedule his sessions with male clients during times when the office is busier, so he feels less isolated. The trauma has also profoundly impacted Kofi’s sleep patterns. Every night, as he lies down to rest, a part of him remains hyperalert, waiting for something bad to happen again. He often finds himself unable to relax and falls asleep only after ensuring that all the windows are locked and the door is barricaded from the inside. This constant state of vigilance has left him exhausted, affecting his concentration at work and overall well-being. Kofi’s sense of safety is deeply compromised, as he feels secure only when his back is against a wall where he can survey the room completely. At home, he positions himself in such a way that he always has a clear view of all entry points, which creates an awkward living arrangement with family and friends visiting. Even at social gatherings, Kofi finds himself constantly scanning the environment for potential threats. On a deeper level, Kofi’s negative appraisals about his own future and his sense of helplessness have taken a toll on him. He has come to believe that he has no future and feels powerless to prevent bad things from happening again. This hopelessness is compounded by the feeling that others can see what happened to him just by looking at him, leading him to isolate himself further. Kofi’s avoidance behaviors and hyperalertness have started affecting his professional relationships and work performance. He finds it difficult to engage fully with clients or colleagues due to his preoccupation with safety measures. His growing sense of isolation has also taken a toll on his personal life; he avoids social gatherings and maintains limited contact with friends. What finally brought Kofi to seek help was the realization that these symptoms were not only affecting him but also impacting his ability to practice psychology effectively. He is most afraid of losing control over his life and feeling perpetually unsafe. On the other hand, what he hopes for is a way to reclaim his sense of security and regain a semblance of normalcy in his daily life. Kofi recognizes that the trauma has left him with significant emotional wounds that require professional intervention to heal. Through therapy, Kofi seeks support in managing his triggers, reducing hypervigilance, and addressing his negative appraisals. He hopes to find ways to reconnect with others and rebuild a sense of safety both at work and in his personal life.
